headline: When QQQ's RSI Hits 81, the Easy Money Is Gone
lede: The Invesco QQQ Trust closed at a record $711.23 on May 8, 2026, its sixth consecutive weekly gain, after staging the fastest oversold-to-overbought reversal in forty years of Nasdaq-100 data. By May 6, the fund's 14-day daily RSI had reached 81.56 — a level that trader @jablamsky, cataloguing every comparable instance since 2014, argues has reliably marked the point where risk-reward deteriorated for bulls. His thesis is probabilistic: RSI 80+ does not guarantee a correction, but it shifts the burden of proof.
body:
The path to RSI 81 was itself exceptional. U.S.-Israeli military strikes on Iran in late February 2026 sent Nasdaq-100 stocks into correction territory; the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) had its *RSI* fall to 28 on March 30 — deeply oversold. When ceasefire news broke in early April, the fund reversed so sharply that it completed the oversold-to-overbought cycle in eleven trading sessions, shattering the prior forty-year record of twenty sessions. April became the Nasdaq 100's best month since the pandemic.

@jablamsky's thread catalogues every instance since 2014 when QQQ's daily RSI touched 81+, arguing that each one eventually gave way to a meaningful correction. The one data point visible in the truncated tweet — Summer 2024, where QQQ ran another 5% before correcting roughly 15% — is consistent with what analysts call *momentum exhaustion*: latecomers push price into extreme territory while early-cycle buyers quietly distribute. The poster's framing is deliberately restrained: RSI 80+ “doesn’t guarantee a deep correction,” but **the burden of proof is on the bulls**.

The counterargument is serious. In genuine bull markets, RSI routinely stays elevated for weeks to months without triggering a reversal; the indicator measures intensity of momentum, not its direction. An event study of 44 instances where the Nasdaq 100 gained 11% or more in ten sessions found average 12-month forward returns of +24%, with a 69% win rate. The current backdrop — AI infrastructure demand, the Iran ceasefire, and tariff uncertainty contained — provides coherent fundamental underpinning. Probability-weighted, further gains remain more likely than not; the danger lies in the tail, where the rare bad outcomes have historically been severe.

What the thread really offers is a regime framing. Options market data as of May 6 showed put volume (3.57 million contracts) outpacing call volume (2.92 million) over the trailing ten days — a sign that institutional holders were hedging even as QQQ printed new all-time highs. RSI at 81 does not tell you when the rally ends. It tells you the room is very crowded, and the exits are the same size they always were.

concepts.definition: A momentum oscillator developed by J. Welles Wilder in 1978. It compares average gains to average losses over the prior 14 sessions and produces a bounded score from 0 to 100. Readings above 70 are conventionally 'overbought'; analysts working with high-momentum instruments often raise that threshold to 80, filtering for only the most compressed, one-sided rallies.

A technical condition in which an asset's price has risen so sharply that momentum indicators exceed a set threshold, suggesting buying pressure has become extreme. It describes intensity, not direction — in strong uptrends, assets can remain overbought for weeks or months before correcting. It is a necessary but not sufficient condition for a top.

The late phase of a rally when the pool of willing new buyers has shrunk to the point where further price gains require progressively more effort. Often visible as RSI at an extreme level with slowing volume or narrowing breadth. It signals deteriorating risk-reward rather than an imminent reversal.

A stock market index of the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the NASDAQ exchange, weighted by market capitalisation. Dominated by mega-cap technology companies, it is the primary benchmark for U.S. large-cap growth investing. The QQQ ETF is its most widely traded proxy.

A complete RSI round-trip from below 30 (oversold) to above 70 (overbought). Tracking the speed of this journey is one way analysts gauge the ferocity of a market reversal. The Nasdaq 100 historically completes this cycle in roughly 67 trading sessions on average; doing it in 11, as in April 2026, is unprecedented in forty years of data.

fact_check: The tweet cites a Summer 2024 episode in which QQQ 'ran another 5%, then corrected 15%' after RSI hit 81+. This is directionally consistent with known QQQ price history — the fund peaked near $510 in July 2024 before a sharp technology-sector selloff — but the specific percentages could not be independently verified from primary sources consulted. Treat the figures as approximate. The full list of RSI 81+ instances going back to 2014 was also unavailable for verification, as X.com returned an authentication wall for the thread URL.
thread_summary: The thread catalogues every instance since 2014 in which QQQ's daily RSI exceeded 81, arguing that in each case a meaningful correction followed, even when price first extended further. Only the first data point — Summer 2024: approximately +5% then -15% — was visible in the available tweet text; the full numbered list was not recoverable because X.com requires authentication to view the complete thread. The thread's conclusion is probabilistic: RSI 81+ does not guarantee a crash, but the historical record consistently places the burden of proof on bulls.
